title: Lab size, from everyone alone to one lab of everyone, on a graph where deeper ideas are much harder (4 bits per level)
html:
Lab size, from everyone alone to one lab of everyone, on a graph where deeper ideas are much harder (4 bits per level)

Question: On a graph where deeper ideas are much harder (4 bits per level), with 24 agents in labs of 1 to 24 that share inside the lab, how much money does the field need, against OSO across the whole field?

Answer: At budgets 32–64: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits) and knowledge per unit of money; clearly worse on waste; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value and ROI. At budgets 128–512: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value and ROI. At budget 1024: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budgets 2048–4096: best Labs of 24 (one lab of everyone). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budgets 8192–16384: best Labs of 24 (one lab of everyone). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste. At budget 32768: best Labs of 24 (one lab of everyone). Against traditional, clearly better on targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level and knowledge found (bits). Design (fixed before the run): compared labs of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 against field-wide OSO at α = 0.8 and 0.2, by budget · held the same: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 24 identical agents, budget 75 split equally, no mint, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 30 graphs × 5 runs on each, per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model with 24 identical agents on a graph where deeper ideas are much harder (4 bits per level), 6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, composition 0.7; each graph run 5 times. Traditional rules (α = 1, nothing published before a target), with agents in equal labs of 1 (alone), 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 (one lab of everyone); lab mates share every proof at once, privately. Against OSO across the whole field at α = 0.8 and 0.2. Held fixed: equal money per agent every round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
